memory_annotations.evidence_summary: No durable hotel-room bed policy was evidenced in this session because Avery is traveling alone for work; the selected king room is a trip-specific inventory choice outside the shared personal-room policy scope.

messages.content: Now I need the hotel for Tuesday, October 14 through Saturday morning, October 18. The approved cap is $265 per night before tax. I need the first trip to the museum to be straightforward for the 7:00 a.m. installation call on Wednesday.

I’ll compare four-night availability with an emphasis on an easy early-morning route downtown. Is the cap strictly the room rate, or do mandatory destination fees also need to fit within $265 per night?
Mandatory fees count toward the cap. Taxes can be added afterward. I’d rather not depend on a bus transfer that early.

Three available options fit those terms. The Palmer House has a standard room at $238 plus a $20 mandatory nightly fee, about a 12-minute walk to the museum. The Silversmith has a standard room at $249 with no mandatory fee, about a 9-minute walk. The Central Loop Hotel is $221 with no mandatory fee, roughly a 14-minute walk. All three allow checkout Saturday morning.
What are the cancellation terms and totals with tax? The Silversmith sounds most practical so far.

For October 14-18, the Silversmith flexible rate totals $1,153.84 including estimated taxes. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. local time on October 13; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. The Palmer House totals about $1,199.20, and the Central Loop Hotel about $1,024.36. Both also have flexible cancellation, but their deadlines are October 12.
Check the actual room category at the Silversmith. I don’t want a listing that turns out to be an accessible room someone else may need, and I need a desk for reviewing condition reports.

The quoted option is a standard non-accessible Deluxe King room. It lists a writing desk, desk chair, in-room safe, and complimentary Wi-Fi. An accessible room is shown separately and is not part of this selection.
Is the walk well lit at that hour, and is there a simple fallback if the weather is bad?

The walking route stays on major downtown streets and is about half a mile. Before dawn, a taxi or rideshare is the simplest fallback; the drive is typically around 5 to 10 minutes, though pickup and traffic can vary. The hotel front desk can also arrange a cab.
That works. Before booking, verify there isn’t a lower rate that becomes nonrefundable or excludes Wi-Fi.

There is a $226 advance-purchase rate, but it is fully nonrefundable from the time of booking. Wi-Fi is included on both rates. Given the exhibition schedule, the $249 flexible rate preserves the useful cancellation window and remains under the $265 cap with no mandatory fee.
Use the flexible rate. Reserve the Deluxe King for four nights on the employer travel card already in my profile. Put only my name on the room.

The reservation is ready to submit for one guest, October 14 check-in and October 18 checkout, at the flexible rate of $249 per night before tax, with an estimated total of $1,153.84. The cancellation deadline is 6:00 p.m. Chicago time on October 13. Shall I complete it?
Yes, complete it and give me the confirmation details in a compact form.

Booked: Silversmith Hotel Chicago, Deluxe King, one guest, four nights. Check-in Tuesday, October 14; checkout Saturday, October 18. Flexible rate: $249 nightly before tax; estimated total $1,153.84. Free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. local time October 13, then a one-night-plus-tax penalty. Confirmation: SHC-481726. The museum is approximately a 9-minute walk, with taxi or rideshare as the early-morning weather fallback.
